paper_metadata.title: A 6-bit 1.2-GS/s Low-Power Flash-ADC in 0.13-m Digital CMOS
paper_metadata.abstract: We present a 6-bit 1.2-GS/s flash-ADC with wide analog bandwidth and low power, realized in a standard digital ADCs employ resistive interpolation and averaging requiring a 0.13 m CMOS copper technology. Employing capacitive interdedicated sample-and-hold at the converter input, the capacitive polation gives various advantages when designing for low power: interpolation structure with distributed front-end sample-andno need for a reference resistor ladder, implicit sample-and-hold hold has advantages in terms of power, even at GS/s speed. The operation, no edge effects in the interpolation network (as comoutstanding figure of merit (FoM) numbers prove the efficiency pared to resistive interpolation), and a very low input capacitance of only 400 fF, which leads to an easily drivable analog converter of the implemented architecture, when compared to state-ofinterface. the-art 6-bit flash ADCs.
